reasoning_traces.think:
The core methodology combines stratified sampling to construct playing XIs, then models each player’s score using a gamma distribution parameterized from historical opponent-specific data. These scores are summed across players to simulate team totals, repeated 10,000 times to compute win probabilities. The approach assumes independence of player scores and uses empirical Bayes to estimate parameters rather than full Bayesian updating. This structure maps directly to GSE’s lineup generation and GSI’s predictive modeling pipelines. Failure modes include poor gamma fit due to non-stationary performance trends, insufficient historical data for rare matchups, and violation of independence assumptions in partnerships or batting order effects. The method’s strength lies in its robustness to out-of-sample prediction when properly validated.
